name: Saint James
why: The Breton stripe, from the Normandy town that gave it its name.
origin: Saint-James, Normandy — the company formally became Société Anonyme des Filatures de Saint James in 1889, spinning wool for sailors and fishermen. Employee-owned since 1990.
opview: Presents itself as the Normandy house that clothed sailors and fishermen, employee-owned and still making in France.

onething.p: The marière, the Breton striped shirt
onething.n: verified — the house's own history page dates the garment to the town and the sea, and it remains what it is bought for

notes.wool: 28 of 67 clothing styles are wool-dominant — the house began as a spinner
notes.fren: Saint-James in Normandy is the town, the company and the garment
notes.boat: the marière is working sailors' kit rather than yacht-club dress

marks: A HOUSE technical material with its own coined name: UVYL. Declared verbatim on the brand's own fabric guide - 'Anti-UV UVYL. What is UVYL?
